statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: When a UAC wishes to terminate a call before it has been answered, it sends CANCEL.
statements.trigger: UAC wishes to terminate call before answered

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If the original INVITE still returns a 2xx, the UAC then sends BYE.
statements.trigger: 2xx received for INVITE after CANCEL sent

statements.subject: session
statements.description: BYE can only be sent on an existing call leg (now called a dialog in this RFC).
statements.guard_semantics: BYE may only be sent within an established dialog

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: When a user sends an INVITE and then a CANCEL, the INVITE transaction still terminates normally.
statements.trigger: CANCEL sent for in-progress INVITE transaction
actions: INVITE transaction terminates normally (independently of CANCEL transaction)

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A UAS needs to respond to the original INVITE request with a 487 response.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: RFC 2543 allowed the UAS not to send a response to INVITE when a BYE was received. That is disallowed here. The original INVITE needs a response.
statements.trigger: BYE received during active INVITE transaction

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A UA cannot send a BYE for a call until it has received an ACK for the initial INVITE.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A UA or proxy cannot send CANCEL for a transaction until it gets a provisional response for the request.
statements.trigger: UA or proxy wishes to send CANCEL

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: It is allowed for non-INVITE requests [to initiate a new transaction to a peer while another is in progress], disallowed for INVITE.
statements.guard_semantics: A UA cannot initiate a new INVITE transaction while another INVITE transaction is in progress; non-INVITE concurrent transactions are allowed

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Proxies no longer forward a 6xx immediately on receiving it. Instead, they CANCEL pending branches immediately. In all cases except this race condition, the result will be the same - the 6xx is forwarded upstream.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In RFC 2543, a proxy was not required to forward provisional responses from 101 to 199 upstream. This was changed to MUST.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: receipt of a 503 should trigger an attempt to contact the next element in the result of a DNS SRV lookup.
actions: attempt contact with next element from DNS SRV lookup result
